environment.note: single host; headless Playwright Chromium logged in through the real login form and drove the real desktop shell

launch.method: start-menu tile click (menu already open, excluded) -> first adopted RAST window (`linux:<app>:<wid>`); cold = user session stopped first, warm = shared session kept and only the app restarted; firstPainted = additional time until the adopted window's pixels change

inputLatency.method: keydown (Node Date.now) -> first changed screenshot pixel of the adopted app window; includes Playwright/Chromium/Xpra encode and the public-URL round trip; upper bound, resolution = poll granularity

typingBurst.method: type 40 chars with Playwright delay=0; dispatch = first key -> last key written; drain = last key -> first stable (two identical) screenshot after the burst; total = first key -> stable frame; screenshot polling ~35 ms + round trip, so drain/total are upper bounds

direct.note: raw Xpra HTML5 session page opened directly (desktop shell and window manager excluded)

notes: All timings are taken in the Node process with Date.now(); the browser and the RAST server are on the same host but --base-url defaults to the public HTTPS URL (Cloudflare/nginx path), which is the intended production measurement.
Input latency and typing-burst drain are upper bounds: the display is sampled with screenshots, so the reported resolution is the poll granularity below.

Scrolling/animation/video FPS are reported three ways: distinct CDP screencast frames (painted compositor frames), distinct fixed-interval screenshots (lower bound), and server-side encoded frames from xpra info deltas.

The app window for the interaction phases is resized through the native shim to 1440x860; the benchmark page is served by this harness on 127.0.0.1 and loaded inside the remote Chrome through its own address bar.
CPU/memory come from cgroup v2 of the user's rast-xpra-u<id> session unit plus every active rast-app-* unit of that identity.
Bandwidth counts WebSocket payload bytes of the Xpra HTML5 client as observed by Playwright (application-level, after Xpra compression); it includes all channels of the session.
The harness only touches the benchmark user's own session through the RAST API; it never stops systemd units or production services directly.
